items.abstract: The thermal conductivities of (001) $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films deposited on $c$-plane sapphire substrates were measured with frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR). The thermal conductivity increases from 1.83 $^{+0.19}_{-0.18}$ W/m$\cdot$K to 2.26 $^{+0.35}_{-0.40}$ W/m$\cdot$K as the thicknesses increase from 159 nm to 689 nm. This weak thickness dependence indicates that the majority of the intrinsic phonon mean free paths are smaller than the range of investigated film thicknesses. First-principles-based calculations that include phonon-phonon and phonon-boundary scattering capture this size-dependent behavior and support our experimental observation. Temperature-dependent measurements of a 689 nm film from 293 to 400 K show a decrease in thermal conductivity with increasing temperature due to enhanced phonon-phonon scattering. A weaker temperature dependence is observed in a 159 nm film where phonon-boundary scattering becomes more prominent. At comparable film thicknesses, our measured $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ films exhibit lower values of cross-plane thermal conductivity than the other experimentally measured Ga$_2$O$_3$ polymorphs. Our experimental observations are supported by prior predictions, which suggest that the low thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ results from its complex crystal structure, which leads to increased anharmonicity and lower phonon group velocities relative to other polymorphs. Thermal management strategies, such as integration with high-thermal-conductivity substrates, may thus be required to mitigate self-heating for $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$-based electronic devices.
items.title: Low cross-plane thermal conductivity of $κ$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ thin films

items.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now approach density functional theory (DFT) accuracy at a fraction of its cost, but the practical benefit is limited by software fragmentation: each state-of-the-art architecture is released as a separate codebase, with its own data format, configuration system, training loop and molecular-dynamics interface. Comparing two architectures on the same dataset, or moving a trained model into a production simulation, therefore requires substantial re-engineering. We introduce IANN (InterAtomic Neural Network), an open-source PyTorch framework that reimplements equivariant graph neural networks - PaiNN, NequIP, MACE, Allegro, EquiformerV2, EquiformerV3 and UMA - behind a unified data object, a unified trainer and a single deployment route, so that the architecture is a one-word change in a configuration dictionary. Forces, stresses and virials are obtained for every architecture from one analytic differentiation of the energy with respect to the edge vectors of the atomic graph, exact under periodic boundary conditions. Distributed training is configured automatically from the SLURM, PBS or MPI environment, so the same script runs unchanged from a workstation to a multi-node GPU allocation. Self-describing checkpoints serve directly as ASE calculators, as ensembles reporting uncertainties, or as TorchScript models run inside LAMMPS through bundled C++ pair styles with single- and multi-GPU inference. Trained on a common dataset of millions of structures, the architectures can be compared under identical conditions. We further release PaiNN foundation models trained on 41.9 million curated DFT structures from MPtrj, Alexandria, OMat24, MatPES, OC20, OC22, OC25, MPr2SCAN and MatPESr2SCAN, spanning the PBE, RPBE and r2SCAN…
items.title: IANN: A Unified Framework for Equivariant InterAtomic Neural Networks with User-Friendly Implementation

items.abstract: ABSTRACT Thermal management materials face a persistent challenge: high thermal conductivity ( κ ) and low Young's modulus (E) are often mutually exclusive. Stiff materials typically conduct heat well while compliant materials tend to thermally insulate. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer exceptional structural tunability that breaks this trade‐off, yet a systematic understanding of κ ‐E decoupling remains elusive. Here we establish an interpretable machine learning framework integrating molecular simulations, six benchmarked models, and SHAP‐based feature analysis to screen over 52 000 topologically valid three‐dimensional COFs. Using random forest as the optimal model, we identify 26 COFs that simultaneously achieve high κ (> 0.8 W m − 1 K − 1 ) and low E (< 8 GPa), a combination difficult to attain by conventional design. SHAP analysis reveals that decoupling arises from nonlinear cooperative actions of multiple descriptors rather than single‐feature tuning. Phonon‐level transport analyses show that intermediate density, strong covalent connectivity, moderate porosity, and low linker fragment complexity balance volumetric heat capacity, phonon group velocity, and phonon lifetime, enabling high κ while preserving low E. This work provides a blueprint for thermally conductive yet mechanically compliant COFs and establishes a generalizable workflow for exploring property decoupling in framework materials.
items.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Reveals Design Rules for Thermal‐Mechanical Decoupling in Covalent Organic Frameworks

items.abstract: Predicting metastable states with universal machine-learned interatomic potentials requires that they preserve the minima and saddles of the reference potential-energy surface. Here we identify local topology hallucination, in which distinct model minima relax into the same reference basin. This failure arises from mode-selective curvature-sign errors shared by MACE, CHGNet and M3GNet. Curvature signs predicted by two of the three models agreed with density-functional calculations in 55 of 57 positive but only 5 of 56 negative cases. In LiGe$_2$S, two MACE minima connected by a verified saddle relaxed into one density-functional basin. Reference relaxation likewise returned nine of ten selected model minima to their reference basins. A directional test with two displaced reference calculations rejected 9 of 12 prospectively tested model instabilities. Model agreement alone therefore cannot establish that predicted minima are distinct metastable states.
items.title: Local topology hallucinations in universal machine-learned interatomic potentials

items.abstract: The intrinsic thermal conductivity ($κ$) of graphene remains highly controversial because of physical and metrological complexities. Although the thermal bridge method enables reliable measurements, sample fabrication remains challenging. Here, we develop a highly efficient patterning and transfer technique to systematically fabricate and characterize suspended bilayer graphene (BLG) thermal bridges with lengths of 1-30 $μ$m. Suspended BLG with unavoidable polymer residues exhibits length-independent thermal conductivity of approximately 570 W/(m K) at room temperature, remaining nearly constant from 250 to 350 K and robust to rigorous surface cleaning and amorphous silicon nitride substrates. Homogeneous non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (HNEMD) simulations show that amorphous carbon coverage of only approximately 0.01 monolayer is sufficient to suppress out-of-plane flexural acoustic (ZA) phonons. These findings challenge the prevailing view that rigid substrates suppress ZA phonons more strongly than surface contamination and identify a robust lower bound of $κ$ governed by amorphous surface scattering. This lower bound reflects heat conduction in graphene under realistic device conditions and provides a reference for fundamental phonon transport studies and the integration of graphene into thermal management applications in electronic devices and chips.
items.title: Lower Bound of Thermal Conductivity in Graphene

items.abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer near–ab initio accuracy at a fraction of the cost of conventional electronic structure calculations, but their reliability depends critically on the quality and diversity of training data. Here, we present a classical-to-density functional theory (DFT) multi-fidelity workflow for efficient dataset generation, in which long classical molecular dynamics trajectories are supplemented with selectively DFT-optimized configurations to train neural network potentials. We demonstrate this approach on four systems: bulk water, water at the air–water interface, CaSO4 in bulk water, and CaSO4 at the interface. In all cases, the trained models faithfully reproduce reference DFT properties, validating the workflow across both simple and chemically complex environments. We further probe the extrapolation capabilities of the models, showing that bulk-trained networks can generalize to different temperatures, pressures, and interfacial geometries when datasets include targeted augmented configurations. This multi-fidelity strategy thus enables accurate and transferable MLIPs for complex solvated and interfacial systems, bridging the gap between computational efficiency and first-principles accuracy.
items.title: Classical-to-DFT multi-fidelity approach for developing machine learning potentials of aqueous systems

items.abstract: This work presents a single-event radiation-hardened p-GaN gate high electron mobility transistor with a grounded Schottky contact (GSC-HEMT). A Schottky contact connected to the source electrode is fabricated on the barrier layer between the gate and drain terminals. Under Ta ion irradiation with a linear energy transfer of 82.06 MeV cm2/mg, the GSC-HEMT exhibits a significantly enhanced single-event burnout (SEB) voltage of over 500 V, demonstrating excellent SEB tolerance. In the conventional p-GaN HEMT, irradiation-induced holes accumulate beneath the gate region, resulting in a larger local electric field and increased gate leakage current. The proposed GSC-HEMT is capable of rapidly collecting irradiation-induced holes through its grounded Schottky contact. This structure can effectively suppress the massive accumulation of positive charges under the gate and within the buffer layer, thereby improving the radiation tolerance of the device. The designed device demonstrates great application prospects in aerospace electronics.
items.title: Irradiation-hardened p-GaN HEMTs achieving >500 V single-event burnout hardness at 82.06 MeV cm2/mg

items.abstract: We report an unusual nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the optical band gap in the layered nitride halide TiNCl, revealed by temperature-dependent photoluminescence (PL) and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy. The band gap, determined from the PL spectra, decreases with increasing temperature at low temperatures, reaches a minimum near 50 K, and then increases at higher temperatures. This behavior contrasts with the monotonic decrease typically observed in conventional semiconductors. The observed temperature dependence is well reproduced by a Bose-Einstein oscillator model with two characteristic phonon energies of approximately 8.9 meV and 1.2 meV. Based on temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction measurements and first-principles calculations using the experimental lattice parameters, we found that the contribution of thermal expansion is negligibly small compared with the observed band-gap variation. Furthermore, first-principles phonon calculations for the optimized crystal structure revealed peaks in the phonon density of states near these two characteristic energies. These results suggest that electron-phonon interactions play an important role in the anomalous temperature dependence of the optical band gap in TiNCl, with low- and higher-energy phonons contributing to the low-temperature decrease and the higher-temperature increase, respectively.
items.title: Anomalous temperature dependence of the band gap in TiNCl

items.abstract: Atomistic foundation models have emerged as a promising route to DFT-level accuracy for materials simulation with complex chemical environments. However, their reliability across competing bonding regimes and, more importantly, how complex bonding affects predictions of material properties remain unclear. Among materials with competing bonding regimes, sodium storage in hard carbon poses a substantial challenge. Hard carbon features diverse local structural motifs, including defective and curved graphitic regions, amorphous regions, and closed/open pores. Motivated by its importance for Na-ion batteries, we systematically evaluate existing pretrained foundation models based on the MACE architecture across different local Na/C motifs. We find that the pretrained models fail to accurately capture Na-Na and Na-C interactions for metallic Na clusters on graphene. To recover a DFT-level energetic description, we employ targeted fine-tuning, showing that it can describe the energetic stability of local motifs and achieve sufficient transferability to unseen Na/C environments. With the developed fine-tuned model, we establish a correlation between closed-pore radius in hard carbon and plateau voltage, showing that the small pores contribute at larger voltages than large ones, suggesting thus how the developed fine-tuned foundation model can link atomistic information with materials design for complex bonding environments.
items.title: Fine-tuned atomistic foundation model for accurate sodium-carbon chemistry in Na-ion batteries

items.abstract: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm$^2$/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm$^2$/s). The monolayer anisotropy is smaller than the calculated exciton dispersion alone would suggest, which first-principles calculations attribute to preferential exciton-phonon scattering to large momenta along the zigzag direction. These directly measured, layer-resolved diffusivities identify armchair-aligned monolayers as the optimal geometry for directional transport and show that transport anisotropy cannot be inferred from band dispersion alone.
items.title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus

items.abstract: In this work, the mechanism of single-event burnout (SEB) in p-GaN gate HEMTs is thoroughly investigated by irradiation experiments and simulations. The samples were irradiated with tantalum (Ta) ions (67 MeV cm2/mg in GaN). There are two distinct failure modes observed in samples occurring in SEB. One is the four-terminal short-circuit mode, and the other is the vertical short-circuit mode between the drain and the substrate. By comparing damaged structures, it can be inferred that both failure modes probably originated from the burnout of the drain. According to the transient currents and temperature distributions by simulations, it is found that the most sensitive region to SEB is the edge of the drain, rather than the edge of the gate or field plate. The SEB mechanism can be explained as follows. A large number of generated holes accumulate at the GaN/AlN interface, while a large number of electrons will accumulate at the Si-Sub/AlN interface, leading to a high electric field in the AlN layer and in turn enhancing the impact ionization. Then the generated electrons will drift to the drain and concentrate around the drain, which produces high current density as well as a high electric field near the drain. Therefore, the lattice temperature there is quickly raised to trigger thermal runaway at the drain.
items.title: Investigation of single-event burnout mechanism in p-GaN gate HEMTs

items.abstract: Energy landscape exploration requires extensive energy and force evaluations, making efficient access to interatomic potentials an important practical challenge. We present a persistent socket interface that connects the landscape exploration tools in the GMIN, OPTIM, and PATHSAMPLE programs to potentials available through the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE). The persistent design keeps both the calculator and socket connection active throughout the search, avoiding repeated initialisation. We apply this framework to understand and predict the properties of Ga vacancies in $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ using two NequIP-based potentials, and construct kinetic transition networks describing complex vacancy configurations and migration pathways. Temperature-dependent analysis of the dominant paths reveals how the most probable migration sequence can change, with the mechanism governed by global properties of the network, rather than simply the highest energy barrier. Visualisation, mean first-passage times, and heat capacities enable us to connect the organisation of the landscape to relaxation time scales and thermodynamic observables. The interface extends energy landscape methods to ASE-compatible atomistic models, providing a general framework for combining global optimisation, transition state searches, kinetic network analysis, and thermodynamic characterisation with recent developments in machine-learned interatomic potentials.
items.title: Exploring Energy Landscapes for Functional Materials: Ga vacancies in $β$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$

items.abstract: First-principles calculations implicitly encode bonding and charge transfer, but converting periodic electronic structure into interpretable and transferable descriptors remains challenging. Recently, we introduced Crystal Orbital Guided Iteration To atomic-Orbitals (COGITO), a tool for mapping plane-wave DFT back to an interpretable, minimal basis of adaptive atomic orbitals. Here, we show how the high-dimensional bonding information from COGITO can be reduced into chemically useful descriptors of covalent bonding, charge transfer, and crystal-dependent atomic chemistry without collapsing the real-space origin of the interactions. Compared to methods that use static or orthogonal orbital bases, COGITO descriptors of short- and long-range bonding show more stability and a better ability to distinguish between ionic, covalent, and metallic bonding regimes. Lastly, COGITO reliably decomposes band dispersion into range-resolved contributions, allowing us to verify and add to the orbital origins of silicon's low-symmetry conduction band minimum. Overall, the adaptive COGITO-based descriptors encode electronic structure, offering a well-structured route to expose the orbital interactions and charge transfer responsible for electronic properties.
items.title: Adaptive nonorthogonal atomic orbitals refine charge transfer and bonding descriptors

items.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) show promise for predicting materials properties, but interpretability remains a challenge, particularly understanding whether attributed feature importance reflects physical reality or statistical artifacts. Here, we present a methods validation study that deliberately overfits a physics-aware GNN ensemble to probe the robustness of feature-ranking approaches. Using the CoMoFeNiCu high-entropy alloy system with three stoichiometries, we train GNNs to predict decomposition enthalpies from DFT-calculated structures while explicitly constraining output weights to encode feature importance. By design, our dataset is limited (approximately 900 binary and 4,500 ternary decomposition pathways) to control compositional complexity and enable precise interrogation of local chemistry effects. We validate that feature rankings capture meaningful local-environment information through a series of atomic swap perturbations: perturbing individual atomic sites and re-ranking features reveals spatial decay consistent with the GNN's interaction cutoff, confirming that weights encode neighbor-shell effects rather than global stoichiometric artifacts alone. Results demonstrate that feature attribution methods can remain physically interpretable even under overfitting, provided validation is rigorous. This work establishes a foundation for trustworthy interpretability in materials GNNs and sets the stage for scaling to multiple chemistries and testing generalization across compositional spaces.
items.title: Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy

items.abstract: Predicting plastic flow in body-centered cubic metals across temperature and strain-rate regimes requires distinguishing structural resistance from kinetic contributions. Here, we develop a temperature dependent mobility law for screw dislocation, integrating thermal activation theory and relativistic effects. Through discrete dislocation dynamics simulations, uniaxial tension and compression simulations were conducted on configurations with different initial dislocation densities, elucidating the correlation between plastic strain rate and key parameters such as stress, temperature, and dislocation density. Subsequently, a unified constitutive model incorporating temperature and strain rate is derived based on microscopic mechanisms. The model naturally bridges microscopic mechanisms to continuum response, resolving the additivity dilemma by establishing explicit physical criteria for how structural resistances and competing kinetic mechanisms superimpose. Through rigorous bottom-up simulations, we quantitatively capture the crossover point where phonon drag overtakes thermal activation, providing a mechanism-based explanation of anomalous thermal hardening. This work enables physically consistent predictions of strength and creep behavior across broad temperature and strain-rate regimes, advancing beyond phenomenological descriptions toward transparent, mechanism-based alloy design.
items.title: Unified constitutive model of body-centered cubic metals informed by discrete dislocation dynamics

items.abstract: We all know how important inspection is for advanced packaging. Not only are these processes critical for ensuring higher yield, but they’re also integral for maintaining device reliability. As the industry pushes for smaller features and tighter spacing, even the smallest defects can pose major challenges. For instance, delaminations and air gaps can be detrimental in a market that demands increasingly complex devices. Such defects will lead to electrical or mechanical failures down the road. One technology that’s mitigating these issues is acoustic micro imaging (AMI). AMI is a high-frequency ultrasound technology, and it’s being used by the industry as an inspection method. How AMI works At the core of AMI technology is a transducer, or a device that turns energy from one form to another. It starts with a pulse of electrical energy, then converts it to mechanical energy, or a high-frequency ultrasound wave. Because ultrasound doesn’t travel through air, this allows inspectors to obtain clear images of gaps and delaminations in the device that could otherwise be difficult to see. However, the transducers used for AMI are not all the same. Each transducer handles a specific frequency, and they’re chosen based on the sample that needs to be inspected. By moving the transducer across the sample, the inspector can generate multiple images that can then be analyzed by the AMI software. Through this analysis, the inspector can choose to accept or reject parts based on the number of defects the package is found to have. So, how do these defects typically present themselves? The biggest difference between ideal and defective samples is that some defective samples will have very clear air gaps. However, another common defect is thinning of the attach material on solder pads.…
items.title: What Is Acoustic Micro Imaging? A Quick Guide To This Inspection Process

items.abstract: Researchers at Arizona State University and Ampere Computing published “DT-MATCH: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield Optimization in Heterogeneous Integration.” Abstract “Heterogeneous integration (HI) and advanced packaging enable chiplet-based system-on-chip (SoC) designs; however, they also introduce new yield challenges arising from manufacturing defects and complex die-to-die (D2D) interconnect constraints. In particular, lane-level defects, limited spares, and strict structural compatibility requirements impede the efficient assembly of functional systems from defective but repairable chiplets. We present DT-MATCH, a defect- and topology-aware chiplet matching framework that maximizes the number of functional SoCs under realistic assembly constraints. DT-MATCH provides two complementary approaches. The integer linear programming (ILP)-based approach is implemented using a batching strategy to approximate the exact formulation. The greedy randomized adaptive search procedure (GRASP)-based approach provides substantial acceleration, but it does not guarantee yield optimality. Both approaches use a preprocessing pipeline to reduce the problem size. Experimental results on industrial designs demonstrate that, as expected, the ILP-based approach achieves superior solution quality. The GRASP-based approach leads to lower runtimes while still achieving solution quality that is comparable to the ILP-based solution. Together, these methods provide a trade-off between solution quality and efficiency for practical chiplet assembly optimization.” Find the technical paper here . November 2026. Xuanyi Tan, Sanmitra Banerjee, Dhruv Thapar, Sreejit Chakravarty, and Krishnendu Chakrabarty. “DT-MATCH: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield…

items.abstract: Documentation: https://alamode-code.github.io/alamode/ Packaging release; the calculations are unchanged. Build / packaging Binary wheels of the Python modules alm and anphon on PyPI for Linux (x86_64, aarch64) and macOS (arm64): pip install "alamode-python[openmpi]" (contributed by Hrushikesh Sahasrabuddhe, GitHub #338 ). The wheels contain neither the command-line programs and tool scripts nor the optional SuiteSparse solvers of alm. The Python distribution is named alamode-python (was alamode , a name that cannot be registered on PyPI). The modules are still imported as alm and anphon . If the Python package of 2.0.0 or 2.0.1 was installed from source, run pip uninstall alamode before installing this version. Boost >= 1.67 is required ( boost::sort::block_indirect_sort ); the build checks and the documentation said 1.66. The Python package requires Python >= 3.11 (was 3.9); it is built and tested with 3.11 and newer only. The Python build can leave out either module ( ALAMODE_PYTHON_ALM=OFF , ALAMODE_PYTHON_ANPHON=OFF ). License texts of the vendored code ( external/LICENSE_1_0.txt , external/niggli_LICENSE.txt ) and of the libraries bundled in the wheels ( python/LICENSES_bundled.txt ). Importing anphon without Open MPI says how to install it.

AI is transforming how we discover, design, and optimize materials, while materials science is simultaneously reshaping the hardware on which AI depends. This Collection captures this bidirectional innovation through the lens of algorithms, platforms, and workflows that enable AI to accelerate materials researchand the materials that, in turn, expand what AI can achieve. Materials science is undergoing a paradigm shift driven by advances in AI and their application to autonomous materials science platforms. The advances in AI are accelerating materials discovery, design, and synthesis through predictive modeling, generative approaches, and autonomous experimentation. Key developments include AI models trained on diverse datasets from high-throughput computation and experimentation; multimodal and generative AI for novel materials and synthesis routes; and autonomous materials science that combines AI/ML with automated laboratories, real-time data analysis, robotic experimentation, and adaptive characterization. Altermagnetism is a recently discovered phase of magnetism characterized by zero net magnetization and strong spin polarization in the electronic band structure. This combination of properties characteristic of elements of both antiferromagnets and ferromagnets arises due to the magnetic sublattices being connected by symmetry operations that are not inversion or translation. The result is a class of materials with a rich array of unconventional magneto-responses, and great technological potential. With this cross-journal collection, the editors at Nature Communications , Communications Materials and Scientific Reports invite submissions on altermagnetic materials. items.abstract: Poster presented at eNergetics 2026, the 6th International Conference on Energy and Environment, 23 to 24 November 2026 (virtual). Cubic CsPbBr₃ is the phase that exists above 403 K, which is the temperature range relevant to waste-heat recovery. Almost all reported measurements, however, are made on the room-temperature orthorhombic polymorph, and while the electronic structure of the cubic phase is established, its lattice dynamics and transport properties are not. This work presents one internally consistent set of first-principles calculations for the cubic phase, covering electronic structure with spin-orbit coupling, optical response, lattice dynamics and thermoelectric transport. Quantities reported here that were not previously available for this phase include the Seebeck coefficient and the thermoelectric figure of merit, the acoustic deformation potentials of both band edges, the R-point soft-mode frequency, and the Debye temperature, sound velocity and Grüneisen parameter. ZT reaches 0.39 at 800 K near 10¹⁹ cm⁻³, with p-type and n-type values equal to within a few percent. Because the lattice thermal conductivity already sits at the Cahill-Pohl glassy minimum of 0.475 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, the ceiling on ZT is set by the power factor rather than by heat transport. Lowering the lattice thermal conductivity further therefore cannot raise ZT in this family, and only the electronic side can be improved. Methods: VASP 5.4.4 with the projector augmented-wave method, PBE and HSE06 functionals and spin-orbit coupling throughout; phonons from finite displacements in a 2x2x2 supercell using Phonopy; electronic transport from BoltzTraP2 within the constant relaxation-time approximation, with the relaxation time taken from Fröhlich polaron theory rather than fitted to experiment.…

items.abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous integration of Gallium Nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) via micro-transfer printing (μTP) offers a scalable route to address critical thermal management and integration challenges for high-power and high-frequency applications. However, traditional polymer adhesives used in the printing process create a thermal bottleneck due to their low thermal conductivity. This work introduces a room-temperature, heatless soldering mechanism at the device level utilizing undercooled liquid metallic core–shell (ULMCS) particles. Synthesized via the shearing liquids into complex particles (SLICE) method, these Field’s metal (Bi/In/Sn) particles are encapsulated in a self-limiting 10 nm oxide shell, maintaining a metastable liquid state until mechanical rupture triggers spontaneous solidification. To test this, GaN/AlGaN coupons were released from Qromis Substrate Technology wafers and printed onto silicon substrates using ULCMS particles. Printing parameters, including shear speed and shear distance, were optimized to ensure consistent adhesion. While initial μTP using compliant polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) stamps achieved high transfer yields, cross-sectional analysis revealed incomplete coalescence due to insufficient pressure applied by the stamp. To resolve this, a dual-stage integration framework was developed, incorporating a secondary rigid glass stamping step. This process successfully created a dense, metallic adhesion layer, providing a robust and cost-effective pathway for the integration of GaN devices for thermal management applications.
items.title: Undercooled Liquid Metallic Core–Shell Particles Enabling Heatless Metal–Semiconductor Bonding for Micro-Transfer Printed GaN

items.abstract: Abstract Eco-friendly Cu3SbSe4 is a promising mid-temperature thermoelectric material. Although Sn-doped Cu3SbSe4 optimizes thermoelectric properties, it also negatively impacts thermal properties. Herein, Cu3Sb0.98Sn0.02Se4-x%PbSe composites were synthesized via an integrated microwave-hydrothermal and spark plasma sintering route. Subsequent characterizations reveal the coexistence of a Cu3SbSe4-based matrix and PbSe secondary phases at higher PbSe contents, while the evolution of the lattice parameters suggests possible partial Pb incorporation into the matrix. The PbSe/Cu3SbSe4 heterointerfaces may contribute to energy-dependent carrier filtering, which is consistent with the enhanced Seebeck coefficient observed after PbSe formation. Concurrently, the coexistence of point defects, grain boundaries, and PbSe-rich regions provides multiple structural features that may contribute to phonon scattering and the evolution of lattice thermal conductivity. First-principles calculations also elucidate that this co-doping strategy fundamentally reconstructs the electronic band structure and phonon dispersion. Consequently, the Cu3Sb0.98Sn0.02Se4-4%PbSe composite delivers a maximum power factor of 999.35 μW m–1 K–2 and a peak zT of 0.77 at 623 K. These results demonstrate that PbSe incorporation provides an additional route for regulating the electrical and thermal transport properties of Sn-doped Cu3SbSe4.
items.title: Synergistic Enhancement of Thermoelectric Properties in Cu3SbSe4 via Multiscale Phonon Scattering and Energy Filtering Effects

items.abstract: ABSTRACT This investigation explores the structural, elastic, electronic, optical, thermal, and thermodynamic properties of silicide compounds (XAl 2 Si 2 , X = Y, La) using density functional theory (DFT). The structural stability and mechanical characteristics were evaluated through elastic constants, micro‐ and macro‐hardness, Cauchy pressure, Pugh's ratio, and Poisson's ratio. The calculated elastic parameters confirm the mechanical stability of both compounds, while the obtained Pugh's ratio, Poisson's ratio, and Cauchy pressure values indicate their ductile nature. Bond population analysis reveals the coexistence of ionic and covalent bonding characteristics. The electronic properties were investigated through band structures and density of states calculations, including spin–orbit coupling (SOC) effects to explore possible topological features. Furthermore, phonon dispersion and thermodynamic analyses were performed to evaluate dynamic and thermal stability. The combination of favorable electrical properties and moderate lattice thermal conductivity suggests potential applications in thermoelectric and high‐temperature environments. Optical investigations reveal that both compounds exhibit reflectance above 75% in the visible region, indicating their capability for reducing solar heat absorption. Additionally, their high refractive index at low photon energies and strong ultraviolet (UV) absorption behavior makes them promising candidates for optoelectronic and UV‐protection applications.
items.title: DFT‐Based Investigation of the Mechanical, Optoelectronic, Bonding, Thermophysical, and Thermodynamic Properties of XAl 2 Si 2 (X = Y, La) Silicides for Potential Applications

items.abstract: ABSTRACT The traditional lone‐pair electron strategy primarily reduces lattice thermal conductivity ( κ L ) by enhancing anharmonic lattice vibrations. However, this mechanism has long been considered to exist only in specific cations with ns 2 electron configurations (e.g. Sb 3+ , Bi 3+ ), severely restricting the broader applicability of this lone‐pair‐based approach. In this study, CuInSnSe 4 is successfully synthesized via atomic cross‐substitution from the diamondoid CuInSe 2 , wherein the Se atoms exhibit an anionic lone‐pair‐like electronic behavior, revealing a new approach to reducing κ L that differs from conventional cation‐based mechanisms. In contrast to the traditional mechanism that relies on cations to enhance lattice anharmonicity, the anionic lone‐pair electrons weaken the Se‐Se interactions, flatten the optical phonon branches, and consequently significantly expand the scattering phase space, providing more scattering channels for phonons. This anionic lone‐pair electron strategy reduces the room‐temperature κ L from 4.48 to 1.26 W m −1 K −1 . Ultimately, the predicted optimal thermoelectric figure of merit ( ZT ) for p‐type and n‐type CuInSnSe 4 attains values of 1.99 and 0.79, respectively. This work systematically expands the conventional application boundaries of the lone‐pair electron strategy and elucidates a fundamentally distinct mechanism for κ L reduction, providing a new theoretical basis for designing and developing novel high‐efficiency thermoelectric materials with intrinsically low κ L .
items.title: Anionic Lone‐Pair‐Like Electrons Induced Ultra‐Low Lattice Thermal Conductivity and High Thermoelectric Performance
